title: Law to ban surveillance pricing
summary: This bill would prohibit businesses from using personal data collected through surveillance technology to set different prices for different customers for the same goods or services, with exceptions for cost-based differences, loyalty programs and discounts for groups like students or seniors. The Department of Consumer and Worker Protection would enforce the law, with civil penalties of $150 for a first violation, $300 for a second and $1,000 for a third or later violation. The law would take effect 120 days after enactment.
